title: Standardize Terraform workspaces and reduce drift noise across VPC templates
creator: Ava Morales
description: Consolidate and standardize Terraform workspace layout and VPC networking templates to reduce state drift noise, make provider upgrades safer, and simplify on-call debugging. This work touches shared modules (vpc, networking-helpers), root workspace patterns used in staging/prod, and CI pipelines that run tf plans on PRs. Objective: reduce noisy plan diffs from non-actionable lifecycle changes, migrate lockfile/provider pinning to a central location, and create a reversible migration path for AWS provider v4 -> v5 in our environments.
acceptance_criteria: All leaf workspaces use the new standardized folder layout and backend config pattern
Terraform plan diffs for unchanged infra should not surface non-actionable lifecycle changes in >90% of PRs
Provider version is centrally pinned in terraform.lock and shared modules reference provider requirements via overrides where needed
State migration steps documented and a staged roll-out (dev -> staging -> prod) executed with a rollback playbook
work_completed: RFC posted: Conventions for workspace layout and provider consolidation (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/TF+Workspace+Conventions
Prototype change to vpc module to stop using computed tags that caused churn (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4121)
Added centralized provider_constraints.tf with pinned checksums and updated CI job to validate terraform.lock per-commit (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4152)
Ran dry-run state copy for dev workspace and validated zero-diff after canonicalizing meta tags (internal run id: dryrun-2026-03-05)
next_steps: Schedule canary provider bump in a single low-traffic region workspace (owner: Jun)
Automate tf plan failure suppression for known harmless lifecycle differences (e.g., aws_route.table_id computed ref) with explicit ignore_changes mapping
Coordinate with platform-oncall for migration weekend and create PagerDuty playbook entry
Add post-migration metrics to Console: plan-diff-frequency and plan-noise-reduction percentage
tradeoffs: We centralize provider pins which reduces per-module flexibility but greatly simplifies upgrades and auditability. Temporary suppression of plan noise risks hiding a genuine drift if the suppression rules are too broad; mitigation is conservative rule scoping and short-lived feature flags in CI. Full provider upgrade may require kernel/runtime changes downstream (e.g., IAM role behavior) — that risk pushes some migration tasks into post-rollout compatibility testing.
